elements.title: Naide Gomes (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Naide Gomes (pictured) broke the Portuguese long-jump record fourteen times in her career, raising it from 6.56 metres to 7.12 metres?

elements.title: Documented (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Documented is the first non-Chinese newsroom in the United States with a WeChat account?

elements.title: Cheng Lianzhen (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Mao Zedong ordered the lenient treatment of bandit leader Cheng Lianzhen, as he thought it rare for a female bandit leader to be from an ethnic minority in China?

elements.title: Seokjojeon (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the building Seokjojeon was meant to symbolize the Korean Empire's authority, but it was completed just months before Japan annexed Korea?

elements.title: Fritz Strassmann (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Fritz Strassmann, a co-discoverer of nuclear fission, concealed a Jewish woman in his home during World War II?

elements.title: thimble cactus (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that thimble cactus is one of the most commonly grown nipple cacti because it breaks into pieces at the slightest touch?

elements.title: Madame Saqui (Wikipedia — did you know?)

elements.title: Didacts and Narpets (Wikipedia — did you know?)
